Title: Father sold car to ease family finances, wins Toyota Vios at Karnival Jom Heboh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A father who had sold his car to ease his family's financial burden ahead of the birth of his second child has struck it lucky, winning a Toyota Vios in a lucky draw at the Jom Heboh Carnival (KJH), held in conjunction with Malaysia Unit Trust Week (MSAM) 2026.
Research officer Akhmalluddin Mohd Sujai, 36, described the win as a blessing for his 4-month-old child.
"Alhamdulillah, I am grateful because I see this as my child's rezeki. Before my second child was born, I had to sell my car.
"I reorganised the finances afterwards. I never expected to receive something even better than the car I sold earlier," he said when met at the daily and grand lucky visitor prize presentation ceremony held in conjunction with KJH x MSAM 2026 at Stadium Merdeka.
The event was launched by Amanah Saham Nasional Bhd (ASNB) chief executive and executive director Fadzihan Abbas Mohamed Ramlee.
A total of 20 winners received prizes, with 33 prizes offered to lucky visitors on the first day of the programme organised by Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) and ASNB.
Akhmalluddin said he entered the lucky draw for fun but also took the opportunity to learn about the investment and financial management products offered at MSAM.
"I came to see what was new, including any new products from PNB or ASNB.
"Yesterday, I was just imagining myself sitting in the car on display. I never expected to be the lucky winner today," he said.
He also praised KJH x MSAM 2026, saying it helped bring financial knowledge closer to the public through a more relaxed, interactive and visitor-friendly approach.
"I would like to thank MSAM, PNB, Sime Darby and all the sponsors, including Jom Heboh, for jointly organising activities to improve financial literacy among Malaysians," he said.
MSAM is also offering grand prizes, including a double-storey terrace house at Suasana Bandar Ainsdale, a BYD Seal Performance electric car and a RM50,000 travel package.
Visitors also stand a chance to win various daily prizes, including a Perodua QV-E, motorcycles and holiday packages, while enjoying more than 150 exhibition and sales booths, interactive activities, meet-and-greet sessions with celebrities, as well as free health and dental screenings throughout the carnival.

Title: 11 undocumented migrants arrested in Shah Alam raid
Article:
SHAH ALAM: Immigration officers arrested 11 undocumented migrants in a raid on an industrial area in Section U4, Shah Alam.
The operation, conducted by the Selangor Immigration Department with Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) and the Sungai Buloh district police headquarters, targeted premises suspected of operating illegally and employing foreign workers without documents.
Selangor Immigration Department deputy director (Control) Mohamad Khusairi Kamarudin said all 11 detainees failed to produce travel documents.
Those arrested were three Bangladeshi men, three Myanmar men and five Myanmar women.
"All of them are being detained under Section 6(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63," he said when contacted yesterday.
MBSA said seven business premises were inspected over breaches of licensing conditions or operating without local authority approval.
Its enforcement department director Sahrul Nizam Ahmad led the inspections.

Title: Fire ravages 4 workers' quarters in Kechau
Article:
KUANTAN: Four workers' quarters at a palm oil mill in Kechau, near Kuala Lipis, caught fire yesterday.
No injuries were reported in the blaze, which broke out about 3pm.
In a statement today, Pahang Fire and Rescue Department assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said two of the semi-permanent terraced houses were completely destroyed, while the other two sustained 80 per cent and 90 per cent damage, respectively.
He said two cars, a Honda Jazz and a Proton Wira, as well as three motorcycles parked at one of the houses, were also destroyed in the fire.
Salahuddin said the department received an emergency call at 3.20pm, and a fire engine from the Kuala Lipis fire station arrived at the scene 18 minutes later.
"Four houses belonging to Kechau Palm Oil Mill, each measuring 20 by 30 feet, were affected by the fire.
"The fire was brought under control at 4pm and the operation ended at 5.36pm," he said.

Title: Anwar asks Loke to resume duties as transport minister
Article:
SEREMBAN:  Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has made clear that he wants Anthony Loke to remain as transport minister.
Anwar said he found it difficult to accept Loke's intention to step down, despite the Seremban MP having his own reasons for doing so.
"I understand, but I have told him that no reason should take precedence over our duty and responsibility to serve the people and the country.
"He is currently on leave, and I want to ask him to resume his duties as soon as possible," he said when opening the state-level Yakin Madani programme at the Paroi Youth and Sports Complex earlier.

Title: Fewer flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak this morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak dropped this morning.
In SELANGOR, the number of flood victims still housed at relief centres fell to 798 people from 247 families, down from 838 people from 256 families yesterday.
According to the Welfare Department's InfoBencana portal, Kuala Langat had the highest number of evacuees, with 735 people sheltering at SK RTB Bukit Changgang, followed by Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu (16) and Kampung Labohan Dagang Community Hall (six).
In Kuala Selangor, one centre remains open, with 41 evacuees placed at Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok.
In PERAK, the number of evacuees sheltering at three relief centres in three districts dropped slightly to 189 people from 55 families, compared with 197 people from 57 families.
The State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) Secretariat said the number of victims at Sekolah Rendah Agama Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung remained at 127 people from 37 families, while the number of evacuees at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council's Dewan Rumah Rehat in Hilir Perak dropped to 55 people from 15 families.
Larut, Matang and Selama saw no change, with seven people from three families still sheltering at SK Batu Hampar.
It is learnt that most of the affected areas are experiencing stagnant floodwaters.
Meanwhile, the Public Works Department said Jalan Padang Serai-Beruas remains closed to light vehicles due to flooding.

Title: Anwar warns of diabetes risks, calls for healthier lifestyles
Article:
SEPANG: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants the public to make sports part of their daily lives and watch their diet to build a healthier population.
He also called on children to pay closer attention to their parents' health, warning that excessive sugar consumption not only affects well-being but also increases healthcare costs, he said.
Anwar said Malaysia's high diabetes rate was worrying despite efforts to promote sports and physical activity.
"Sometimes we remind parents about the diabetes figures, with Malaysia among the highest in Asia. It makes no sense.
"We promote sports and athletics, yet diabetes rates are among the highest. What are the consequences? First, it affects our health and that of our parents.
"Second, the cost of treating the disease increases. If it is caused by hereditary factors or other reasons, I understand. But according to reports, in many cases we bring diabetes upon ourselves. By the time we realise it, it is too late," he said.
The country also faces a
growing childhood obesity problem
, with one in three adolescents overweight or obese, raising concerns about their risk of developing Type 2 diabetes.
He said Malaysians should make sports and physical activity part of their daily lives to build a healthier population.
Under the Malaysia Madani framework, the government focused on development and the economy, but public health was equally important to the country's progress, he said.
"We want everyone to take part in athletics and sports. Only then will the country be healthy.
"What does a Madani nation mean? It means we understand development and the economy are important, but if the people are unhealthy, weak, sluggish, inactive and overweight, how can we progress? Sporting activities must begin," he said.
Anwar was speaking at the launch of the National Sports Day 2026 celebrations at the Sepang International Circuit today.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari and Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Dr Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar were also present.
Anwar also launched the National Sports Industry Plan, aimed at strengthening the sports industry as a driver of economic growth.
The plan was approved by the cabinet in July 2025 following 12 engagement sessions with stakeholders and sports industry players.

Title: Ministry boosts Pedu Dam water storage ahead of expected El Nino
Article:
KUCHING: The Agriculture and Food Security Ministry is increasing water storage at the Pedu Dam in Kedah to ensure sufficient supply for padi field irrigation in the event of an El Nino phenomenon from late next month until April next year.
Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the measure was important to ensure padi cultivation, particularly in the northern states of Peninsular Malaysia, was not affected by water shortages.
He said based on forecasts by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), hot weather was expected to affect several states, including Kelantan, Terengganu, Kedah and Perlis.
"Currently, the water level at Pedu Dam is good, but we want to increase the storage further to ensure sufficient water for padi field irrigation if there is no rain from December to April.
"That is why I was at Pedu Dam two days ago to ensure efforts to increase water storage could be carried out," he told Bernama after attending the Agro Madani Mega Sales @ Medan Niaga Satok 2026 programme here today.
Mohamad also said adherence to the padi planting schedule was important to avoid water shortages while crops were growing, particularly during a prolonged dry spell.
"We also hope all parties, including the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (MADA), ensure that the padi planting schedule is adhered to.
"If planting is not carried out according to schedule, we are concerned that water shortages may occur while the padi is growing," he said.
On preparations for the monsoon season, Mohamad said relevant agencies, including the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the Social Welfare Department and the Education Ministry, were always prepared to deal with possible floods.
However, he said El Nino required a different approach as its effects remained difficult to predict, while flash floods had also become increasingly serious in recent times.
"Rain in Malaysia is nothing unusual... the monsoon season is something we face every year, but El Nino is a relatively new phenomenon that requires different preparations because its effects are still difficult to predict.
"Insya-Allah, the government is always prepared for the monsoon season based on past experience.
"However, El Nino requires a slightly different approach and preparedness measures," he said. — BERNAMA

Title: Sarawak polls: GPS top leaders among 20 candidates returned unopposed
Article:
KUCHING: Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) has so far won 20 seats uncontested during nomination day for the Sarawak election, reports said.
TVS, Suara Sarawak and The Borneo Post reported that those returned unopposed included the two caretaker Sarawak Deputy Premiers, Datuk Douglas Uggah Embas and Datuk Awang Tengah Ali Hasan, in Bukit Saban and Bukit Sari respectively.
GPS information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah also retained his Asajaya seat for a sixth term after being returned unopposed.
Others elected unopposed include Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu vice-presidents Datuk Ibrahim Baki (Satok), Datuk Seri Julaihi Narawi (Sebuyau), Datuk Gerald Rentap Jabu (Layar) and Datuk Len Talif Salleh (Kuala Rajang).
The son of former Sarawak chief minister the late Tan Sri Adenan Satem, Azizul Annuar Adenan, was also returned unopposed in Tanjong Datu.
It was earlier reported that caretaker Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg had won the Gedong seat unopposed.
As of press time, GPS had also secured uncontested wins in Tupong, Bekenu, Kalaka, Repok, Pantai Damai, Samariang, Simunjan, Batang Ai, Lingga, Sadong Jaya and Muara Tuang.
A simple majority in the 82-seat Sarawak Legislative Assembly requires at least 42 seats

Title: Israeli strike kills two Doctors Without Borders staff in Gaza
Article:
JERUSALEM: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) said Saturday an Israeli strike killed two staff members at a clinic in Gaza, with the Israeli army labelling the pair as Hamas fighters.
The Israel Defence Forces (IDF) identified the men, who worked as security guards at the clinic, as Hamas artillery cell commander Moaz Yousef Alitsbach and Ahmed Sufyan Muhammad Ali Abu.
MSF said it was "devastated" by the killings and denounced "a direct hit" on the organisation.
"Our premises were clearly marked with MSF logos, and their location had been communicated to and was known by the Israeli military," it wrote on X.
World Health Organisation chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus slammed the attack.
"Attacks on health facilities, health workers and humanitarian personnel in #Gaza are outrageous and unacceptable," he posted on X.
The IDF denied targeting a hospital or damaging medical infrastructure.
"This is another example of the Hamas embedding itself within international organisations," it posted on Telegram.--AFP

Title: MySiren to undergo simultaneous nationwide test tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The National Early Warning System (MySiren) will be tested nationwide tomorrow from 10.10am to 10.30am to assess its effectiveness in delivering emergency alerts to mobile phones.
MySiren is Malaysia's Early Warning System (EWS), developed to alert the public during emergencies, enabling them to take immediate action to protect lives and property.
The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), through the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) section on its official website, said alerts could be issued for serious threats to life, health, safety or property, including severe weather, floods, tsunamis, major fires, hazardous materials incidents and public safety threats.
According to the FAQ, the nationwide public alert test aims to evaluate the system's performance and identify any technical issues, including how alerts are broadcast and received.
Developed using Cell Broadcast System (CBS) technology, MySiren simultaneously delivers alerts to compatible mobile devices in affected areas via 4G and 5G networks without consuming mobile data.
Unlike the Short Message Service (SMS), which sends messages sequentially to specific phone numbers, the technology enables alerts to be received even during network congestion or when users have exhausted their data quota.
MCMC also encourages users to update their mobile phone operating systems, enable their device software features, restart their phones after updating and ensure that emergency alert settings are activated.
"The minimum device requirements to support EWS alerts are iPhone 11 and newer models running iOS 27.2 or later, Android phones running Android 12 or later, and Huawei devices running EMUI 16 or later, subject to final technical verification," MCMC said.
Authorised disaster management agencies can issue six categories of alerts according to the nature and severity of emergencies, namely National Alert, Extreme Alert, Severe Alert, Missing Person Alert, Test Alert and Exercise Alert.
On Nov 23, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MySiren only delivers notifications to users without accessing the personal data of device owners.
"MySiren differs from SMS, whereby messages are sent to recipients' phone numbers, as the system does not retrieve any information or data from users' devices.
"It also does not involve any cost to recipients," he said.
The alert test aimed to familiarise the public with MySiren's distinctive warning sound, thereby enhancing their emergency preparedness.
Fahmi said MCMC remained the agency responsible for operating MySiren, while authorities such as the police, National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) and local authorities were also granted access to the system.
The development of MySiren began in 2025 at a total cost of RM200 million following an announcement by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling the 2025 Budget in October 2024.
For information and the latest developments on MySiren, visit www.mcmc.gov.my/mysiren and refer to the official communication channels of MCMC, Nadma and other relevant authorities.

Title: Flash floods catch Manjoi residents in Ipoh off guard
Article:
IPOH: With floodwaters rising rapidly around her, Nur Aina Aqilah Hanif, 21, was focused on getting three children under her family's care to safety, including an 11-month-old baby.
Floodwaters from the overflowing Sungai Tapah surged into their house in Jalan Menteri, Kampung Manjoi, reaching chest level within minutes and trapping the family inside after the strong current damaged the kitchen door.
Malaysia is currently in the northeast monsoon season, which began on Oct 27 and is expected to last until March 2027.
The season's initial phase, from November to January, is expected to bring three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain, increasing the risk of flooding, particularly in low-lying areas and near rivers.
Nur Aina said the ordeal began at about 5pm yesterday, when the water rose so quickly they had little time to react.
[[nid:1587524]]
"I had just returned from work. We were terrified because the water rose so quickly. Before we knew it, we were trapped inside and could not even open the door.
"My main concern was the children. There were three of them, including an 11-month-old baby girl. I had to make sure they were all safe," she said when met at her home today.
"The children were crying, but I remained calm.
"I contacted my family through WhatsApp to ask for help. I just wanted someone to rescue us," she said.
Nur Aina said they waited more than 30 minutes before rescuers arrived by boat.
The family had earlier moved their motorcycles and cars to higher ground after noticing the water rising, but the strong current eventually left them helpless.
"This was the worst flood I have ever experienced. I have never been through anything like this.
"At that moment, I was not thinking about our belongings. I just wanted to make sure the children were safe," she said.
Salim Mawar, 71, said floodwaters quickly spilled over the riverbank and into his house, leaving him and his family scrambling to save themselves and their belongings.
[[nid:1587523]]
"It started raining at 4.30pm and the water came in very quickly. Suddenly, we could not do anything.
"When I came outside, the water was already very high. We tried to move the cars and motorcycles, but we did not have enough time. They were eventually submerged.
"We could not save much. The refrigerator, freezer, rice cooker, electrical appliances, clothes and other belongings were all damaged.
"Honestly, I did not even know where to begin because there was so much to throw away," said the retired civil servant.
[[nid:1587522]]
Another resident, Zubairi Soid, 54, said the water was initially ankle-deep at 5.30pm before rising to chest level within a short time.
"I did not expect it to rise so quickly. Before we knew it, the water had reached chest level.
"I have lived here for more than 30 years, and I would say this was the worst flood I have ever experienced," he said.
Zubairi said he hoped the river could be deepened to reduce the risk of flash floods.

Title: Four-way fight awaits DAP's Kelvin Yii in Batu Lintang
Article:
KUCHING: DAP's Bandar Kuching member of parliament Dr Kelvin Yii will face a four-cornered fight in his bid to win the Batu Lintang seat in December's Sarawak election.
Yii will face Gabungan Parti Sarawak's (GPS) See Chee How, Parti Bumi Kenyalang's (PBK) Voon Lee Shan and independent candidate Peter John Jaban.
See won the Chinese-majority seat in the last election on a Parti Sarawak Bersatu ticket before later joining GPS component Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP).
In 2021, See won the seat with a 93-vote majority in a five-cornered fight.

Title: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu's Likud of stalling Israeli coalition talks
Article:
JERUSALEM: Gadi Eisenkot, who is trying to form the next Israeli government, on Friday accused the party of caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of stalling coalition talks in a bid to bring about new elections.
Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party has in recent days agreed coalition deals with two allied parties, but the route to a parliamentary majority is still far from certain.
After the October election failed to deliver a clear majority for either bloc, Yashar has also held talks with Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party over the possibility of forming a national unity government involving both parties.
But no breakthroughs on that front have ostensibly been reached.
"Likud, for its part, was unwilling to compromise and, over two weeks, refused to put a single concrete proposal on the table," Eisenkot said in a statement on Friday.
"Their conduct points to an effort to run down the clock until the mandate expires, split the Change bloc and drag Israel into another election under the outgoing government," he added.
Eisenkot has until Dec 6 – a deadline which can be extended by 14 days – to form a government to replace Netanyahu.
His wide-ranging camp has faced divisions on whether to forge alliances with the ultra-Orthodox parties, or the Arab-majority lists, or whether to form a unity government with Likud.
"We are approaching a moment of decision," Eisenkot said on Friday.
"The question is whether Likud will engage in serious negotiations and commit to a partnership that requires compromise or keep up appearances and continue to stall," he added, but maintained he was still open to talks if Likud was "genuinely prepared to change course."
Likud, in turn, accused Eisenkot of working to form a "dangerous left-wing government" but nonetheless said it would still be open to a unity government.
Eisenkot's Yashar party has so far agreed coalition deals with the left-leaning Democrats party and the right-wing Israel Beiteinu party.
Together, they have a combined total of 36 lawmakers – far short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority.
On Friday, Israeli media reported that Mansour Abbas, the leader of the Arab-Israeli Raam party, was expected the following day to recognise Hamas as a "terror group" – a move that could pave the way for his party to join a possible Eisenkot-led coalition.
But some of Eisenkot's allies have voiced opposition to relying on the support of the Arab-majority lists, which won unprecedented gains in the election.--AFP

Title: China critic in close election race for Taipei mayor
Article:
TAIPEI: Taiwanese people lined up at polling stations across Taipei on Saturday to cast their ballots in a tight mayoral race, as voting got underway in local elections across the island democracy.
China critic Puma Shen is seeking to flip what has long been considered a safe seat for the Kuomintang party (KMT), which favours closer ties with Beijing, and become the capital's first Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) mayor in nearly 30 years.
Taiwan's local elections are held every four years and will decide races for about 11,000 positions, including mayors and magistrates, across the island democracy's 22 cities and counties.
Candidates have campaigned relentlessly for weeks, posing for selfies in night markets, waving from the back of pick-up trucks and appearing on talk shows in a bid to win over voters on issues ranging from transport and childcare to urban renewal.
The government has warned that China has used a range of tactics to try to influence the outcome of the elections, including "cognitive warfare" and "transnational repression".
China claims Taiwan as part of its territory and has threatened to use force to annex the island.
Shen, an academic-turned-lawmaker and expert on Chinese influence operations targeting Taiwan, was the underdog when he entered the race against the more seasoned KMT incumbent Chiang Wan-an, a rising star in his party.
But Shen's savviness on social media and on the campaign trail sparked a frenzy of support dubbed "Ocean Current", a play on his name in Chinese, that spread across the island.
Shen supporter Michelle Wang, 48, said she was initially sceptical of the DPP candidate, but changed her mind after hearing a staunch KMT supporter praise him during the campaign.
"He is just a very polite kid, and later I also learned that he studied very diligently throughout his academic career," Wang told AFP at the polling station where Shen also voted.
"He is practically the ideal good kid in every parent's eyes," Wang said.
"I feel that he is standing in a position leading Taiwan towards a better future, so I think he is a very trustworthy young man."
[[nid:1587475]]
Among the elderly people who arrived early to vote was 82-year-old Chen Sung-sung, who wanted to get it out of the way so he could go hiking.
"Of course I voted for Chiang Wan-an," the sprightly Chen told AFP, describing the mayor as "honest and decent".
"He's done such a good job in Taipei City. Why wouldn't I vote for him?"
'VERY TIGHT RACE'
Polling stations will close at 4pm, with results expected to be released in the evening.
The KMT faces the challenge of defending the 14 city and county seats it won in 2022. President Lai Ching-te's DPP is seeking to improve on the five seats it holds.
Shen, who is also a former civil defence activist, has long been a thorn in the side of Beijing. He is wanted by Chinese police for alleged criminal "separatist activities" and is barred from entering the country.
A Shen victory in the KMT's heartland could be seen as "quite shameful" in Beijing, Austin Wang, a political science professor at the University of Nevada, told AFP ahead of the polls.
Saturday's turnout of undecided and young voters will determine the outcome of the "very tight race", said Liu Jia-wei, a political science professor at National Taipei University.
A major upset could also be brewing in the mayoral election in New Taipei, Taiwan's largest city and another KMT stronghold.
While Taiwan's presidential elections are only 14 months away, analysts have cautioned that the local elections are not a reliable predictor of how people might vote in 2028, with history showing repeatedly that the reverse can happen.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eight killed in Peru military helicopter crash
Article:
LIMA: A Peruvian air force helicopter carrying military personnel crashed in a coca-growing river basin in the country's southeast, killing eight people and seriously injuring the pilot, the defence ministry said Friday.
The helicopter crashed while on a mission to rescue a patrol in a remote area of the valley formed by the Apurimac, Ene and Mantaro rivers, known by its Spanish acronym VRAEM, authorities said.
"Search and rescue operations located the aircraft and the nine military personnel who were on board," the defence ministry said in a statement.
"Enzo Espinoza Roque, the pilot and sole survivor, was evacuated to Lima to receive specialised medical treatment."
VRAEM is Peru's largest coca-growing valley and has been militarised for decades because of drug trafficking and the presence of remnants of the Shining Path guerrilla group.
The aircraft had been reported missing Thursday night after rescuing three army personnel in Sanabamba, a remote community in the Ayacucho region.
No details were given on why they needed rescuing, but they were among those killed in the crash.
Another MI-17 crashed in southern Peru in February killing all 15 on board.
Peru is one of the world's largest producers of coca leaves and cocaine, according to the United Nations.--AFP

Title: Sarawak polls: Abang Johari grateful, some 30 GPS candidates set to win uncontested [WATCH]
Article:
GEDONG: Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg described his
uncontested victory in the Gedong state seat
as a sign of public confidence in the Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) administration.
He said the victory also reflected the people's trust in the state government's efforts to manage Sarawak's development, particularly through the implementation of the Post-Covid-19 Development Strategy (PCDS) 2030.
"I am grateful to Allah, as there are signs of public confidence in Sarawak towards the GPS administration in managing the state's development.
"I also thank the people of Gedong for placing their confidence in me to continue working together on the development plans until 2030," he said.
He said about 30 GPS candidates in several seats had also won unopposed, although the figure was yet to be confirmed.
He said while uncontested victories raised questions about the democratic process, the people's mandate to choose a government capable of administering the state for the next five years remained the priority.
"It is up to the people to place their confidence in the party managing the state.
"Alhamdulillah, it appears that the people of this state want continued development, particularly in Sarawak," he said.
He said continued political stability could boost foreign investors' confidence and encourage Sarawakians to step up economic activities for the state's future.
He also thanked his partners in the unity government for not contesting in Sarawak, saying the move reflected the good understanding between the federal and state governments.

Title: DAP's Chong Jen, Violet Yong face multi-cornered fights in Kota Sentosa, Pending
Article:
KUCHING: The only two DAP leaders who won seats in the last Sarawak election will face multi-cornered fights in December's polls.
In Kota Sentosa, Sarawak DAP chief Chong Chieng Jen will face Gabungan Parti Sarawak's (GPS) Wilfred Yap and Parti Bumi Kenyalang's (PBK) Lue Cheng Hing for the Chinese-majority seat, FMT reported.
Chong, a former Kota Sentosa assemblyman, contested in Padungan in the last election.
Yap, from the Sarawak United Peoples' Party (SUPP), wrested Kota Sentosa from DAP in 2021 after the party had held the seat since 2006.
Meanwhile, Sarawak DAP organising secretary Violet Yong will also face two challengers in her bid to retain Pending.
Yong, who has held the seat for four terms, will face GPS' Wee Hong Seng, who is also Kuching South mayor, and PBK's Tiong Ing Neng.
In the last election, Yong retained the Chinese-majority seat by 540 votes in a five-cornered contest.

Title: Power outage: Police step up security, traffic control in Tawau
Article:
TAWAU: Police have intensified security and traffic control measures in Tawau amid a power outage affecting Sabah's east coast since Thursday.
District police chief assistant commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said maintaining a strong police presence was essential to preventing criminal activities, including cross-border crime and break-ins at commercial and residential premises, particularly at night amid the ongoing power outage.
He said policemen had been deployed to monitor public areas and their surroundings using mobile patrol vehicles and motorcycles.
"As for security deployments along coastal areas, we have engaged the marine police force. The situation remains under control, with no incidents reported so far," he told Bernama.
Rosdi said traffic policemen had also been deployed to manage traffic at affected junctions, with no complaints of congestion received from the public so far.
Traffic lights were not functioning in several areas, including Jalan Sin On and parts of Jalan Apas, while sundry shops, eateries and other businesses had to close early as night fell.
Meanwhile, Rosdi said police were working closely with security agencies and Sabah Electricity to identify areas affected by the power outage, particularly those facing potential security risks.
"We are on standby to deploy personnel and conduct patrols wherever necessary to ensure the safety and well-being of residents," he said.
Rosdi also urged members of the public to report any suspicious activity to the police.
The collapse of tower T313, detected at 6.04am on Thursday, severed two transmission line circuits supplying electricity from Sabah's West Coast to its East Coast, disrupting electricity supply across eight districts and affecting 153,599 registered consumers.
Sabah Electricity is targeting to restore the electricity supply by Dec 2 or earlier.

Title: ECRL expected to boost Kelantan tourist arrivals by 50pct
Article:
KOTA BARU: Tourist arrivals in Kelantan are expected to increase by up to 50 per cent when the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) begins operations next month.
Some tourists are even expected to make day trips to Kelantan to enjoy its food before returning to the Klang Valley in the afternoon or evening, as the journey will take only four hours compared with eight hours by car.
Several sectors, including hotels, homestays, taxi drivers, eateries and handicraft businesses, are expected to benefit from the facility if the visitors are tourists.
Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman and acting Tourism and Arts Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the new service would make it easier for tourists to visit Kelantan.
"We expect tourist arrivals in Kelantan to increase by up to 50 per cent, especially during the initial phase of ECRL operations.
"At the beginning, people will be excited to experience the ECRL service, and it is not impossible that some tourists will arrive in the morning and return in the afternoon or evening.
"We expect ECRL operations to benefit food outlet operators, as many visitors come to Kelantan to enjoy traditional food.
"Meanwhile, transport services are also expected to see increased demand. Homestays and hotels around Kota Baru could also see more bookings if tourists choose to stay overnight," he said.
He reminded traders, particularly food outlet operators, not to take advantage of the expected increase in tourist arrivals by raising prices.
"Do not think that the increase in tourist numbers is an opportunity to raise prices. This is not the right approach. Instead, maintain existing prices if you want to attract tourists and the public over the long term.
"Remember that if tourists are charged exorbitant prices once, they may not return to the same premises. That is why I would like to remind traders not to take advantage of visitors and to maintain cleanliness."
Hilmi said the actual impact of the ECRL on Kelantan, particularly its tourism sector, could only be assessed after the service begins operations.
*New opportunities for taxi drivers
Meanwhile, taxi driver Md Yusoff Ismail, 77, hopes the ECRL will revive the car rental service in Kota Baru, which was once popular about 20 years ago.
He said the new rail service was expected to create opportunities for taxi and rental car drivers to earn an income again, particularly by ferrying passengers from ECRL stations to destinations in and around the city.
"Taxi drivers have been affected since the Covid-19 pandemic, forcing most of them to cease operations as they could no longer afford the cost of living and vehicle maintenance.
"Currently, fewer than 10 taxi drivers remain active in Kota Baru, while the others have surrendered their permits or sold their vehicles to make ends meet.
"With the ECRL beginning operations next month, we hope demand for taxi services will pick up again," he said.

Title: Canada prosecutors seek 25 years for man who sold suicide poison kits
Article:
NEWMARKET: Canadian prosecutors on Friday requested a 25-year prison sentence for a man who sold poison to help people commit suicide, stressing his victims were largely young and experiencing mental distress.
Former chef Kenneth Law pleaded guilty earlier this year to aiding 14 suicides in Canada, but he has admitted to selling hundreds of so-called suicide kits globally through a series of online forums.
Prosecutors had also charged him with murder but, citing a lack of evidence, agreed to withdraw the more serious accusations in exchange for Law pleading guilty to lesser offenses.
That decision drew widespread condemnation, notably from friends and family of victims who believed Law was directly responsible for killing their loved ones, but prosecutors maintained they would still seek a stiff penalty.
"An appropriate global sentence to impose in this matter is 25 years less (time already served)," Crown prosecutor Katie Doherty told the court.
Law's lawyers argued against imposing what could effectively be a life sentence for the 61-year-old.
Law told the court he understood his conduct was "categorically wrong" and that he had been "changed" by the legal process.
"I remain remorseful," he said.
Courts often use comparable cases in determining sentencing, but Doherty noted there is "no case even remotely similar to Mr Law's conduct."
The judge will decide on sentencing on February 26.
- 'VULNERABLE KIDS' -
The Canadian public was shocked when the breadth of Law's operation was revealed following his arrest.
He sold poison to people in at least 41 countries, including China, France, and Brazil. He sold 330 packages to people in the United Kingdom, according to an agreed statement of facts signed by the defence and prosecution. There, 79 deaths are linked to him, according to Canadian prosecutors.
He admitted to entering suicide chat forums under an alias, identifying people considering ending their lives and then directing them to one of his online shops where he sold lethal concentrations of the meat preservative sodium nitrite.
Law sold poison to people who were "just starting off their lives" and "battling mental illness," Doherty said.
That is "a very significant aggravating factor in this case."
Law admitted to aiding the suicide of 21-year-old Stephen Mitchell Jr., whose father was at court on Friday.
This is "an unprecedented case," Stephen Mitchell Sr told reporters on a rainy afternoon outside the courthouse in Newmarket, just north of Toronto.
"But, at its core, it is a person selling a deadly product to vulnerable kids, essentially like my son. That is clearly wrong. That's harming society. That needs to be put to a stop."--AFP

Title: Resignation or not, Anwar tells Anthony Loke to show up for transport minister duty
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 28 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim wants Anthony Loke to resume work as transport minister as soon as possible, saying it is hard for him to accept the DAP secretary-general’s proposal to resign.
Anwar said he respected and understood Loke’s reasons for stepping down, but added that he has asked the latter to return to government work despite that, Bernama reported today in Malay.
“His performance is good and commendable. That is why I, as prime minister, find it hard to accept his proposal to resign,” Anwar was quoted as telling reporters at the Youth and Sports Complex in Paroi, Negeri Sembilan where Loke was also present.
Anwar said Loke is still on leave, but was asked to attend the event because the Transport Ministry is co-hosting it with the Negeri Sembilan government.
Anwar described the Transport Ministry as one of the biggest and most strategic ministries, as it connects the people through air, sea and road infrastructure.
“No reason can override our role in serving the people and the country,” he was quoted as saying.
Loke announced on September 19 that he would resign after the Pardons Board granted former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak house arrest, but he stayed on at Anwar’s request.
He then announced on November 10 that his resignation was effective immediately, after the High Court allowed Najib to serve the rest of his sentence under house arrest.

Title: Selangor flood evacuees fall to 798, Perak down to 189 this morning
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — The number of flood evacuees at temporary relief centres in Selangor and Perak dropped this morning.
In SELANGOR, the number of flood victims still housed at relief centres fell to 798 people from 247 families, down from 838 people from 256 families yesterday.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, Kuala Langat had the highest number of evacuees, with 735 people sheltering at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) RTB Bukit Changgang, followed by Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu (16) and Kampung Labohan Dagang Community Hall (six).
In Kuala Selangor, one centre remains open, with 41 evacuees placed at Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok
In PERAK, the number of evacuees sheltering at three relief centres in three districts dropped slightly to 189 people from 55 families, compared with 197 people from 57 families.
The State Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) Secretariat said the number of victims at Sekolah Rendah Agama Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung remained at 127 people from 37 families, while the number of evacuees at the Teluk Intan Municipal Council’s Dewan Rumah Rehat in Hilir Perak dropped to 55 people from 15 families.
Larut, Matang and Selama saw no change, with seven people from three families still sheltering at SK Batu Hampar.
It is learnt that most of the affected areas are experiencing stagnant floodwaters.
Meanwhile, the Public Works Department said Jalan Padang Serai-Beruas remains closed to light vehicles due to flooding. — Bernama

Title: Walkovers galore for GPS big names, but Dr Sim must fight DAP for Batu Kawah
Article:

Title: Caterer forgot the extra chicken, and the last students in line got it undercooked at Melaka MRSM
Article:
JASIN, Nov 28 — A caterer’s oversight left about 100 pieces of chicken short for fasting students at Maktab Rendah Sains MARA (MRSM) Tun Ghafar Baba here, and some students at the back of the queue were served undercooked chicken recently.
Melaka state executive councillor Datuk Mohd Ridhwan Mohd Ali said a briefing and visit to the school found that the supplier had failed to factor in extra food for students who were fasting, Berita Harian reported today.
“The unexpected situation put pressure on the students, wardens, cooks and the supplier, to the point where the chicken was not fully cooked before it was served,” he was quoted as saying.
He said students who ate early had enough, while those at the end of the queue faced a shortfall.
Mohd Ridhwan, who is also the Ayer Molek assemblyman, said the school quickly provided alternative food that day and no food poisoning was reported.
The matter surfaced after claims went viral that students were served soy sauce chicken that was not fully cooked at dinner.
Students and parents had complained to MARA chairman Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki, who shared the matter on social media with several photos.
Mohd Ridhwan said an internal investigation by the school and inspections by Jasin Municipal Council and Jasin District Health Office officers have been carried out, with several reprimands and internal action taken against the caterer.
He said the health office issued a notice under the Food Act 1983 and Food Hygiene Regulations 2009 over hygiene and food quality, giving the caterer three days to make improvements, including cleaning, before more frequent follow-up inspections.
He said the state government will ask local authorities to step up monitoring, while the school must improve its standard operating procedures for unexpected situations and take students’ complaints seriously.
He urged canteen operators to be more responsible and take food preparation seriously.
“We don’t want something like this to be repeated, especially when some of the students here are about to sit the most important examination of their lives,” he was quoted as saying.
Mohd Ridhwan said further action against the supplier has been left to MARA and the school, in line with the guidelines for appointing suppliers.
He spoke after visiting the school’s dining hall and kitchen yesterday with its management, the council and the health office.

Article:

Title: Zahid hopes exco appointment draws the curtain on Negeri Sembilan crisis
Article:
BAGAN DATUK, Nov 28 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi hopes the appointment of six Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (exco) members yesterday will end the political crisis affecting the state.
Ahmad Zahid, who is also deputy prime minister and Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman, said Umno and BN express gratitude for the consent of the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, on the appointment of the exco line-up.
Ahmad Zahid said the appointment allows the state government to promptly fulfil its responsibilities, including holding a special budget sitting in the State Legislative Assembly and delivering services to the people.
“Most important is the confidence of the people as a whole in the government following Tuanku’s consent, and I am confident the crisis has ended and we hope no new problems will arise after this,” he told reporters after officiating at the 26K Huffaz 2026 Gathering and ‘Bagan Datuk Bermunajat’ event at Masjid Tuminah Hamidi here yesterday.
Ahmad Zahid said five top party leaders had an audience with Tuanku Muhriz on Thursday to seek the best solution for the state’s stability.
The five were Ahmad Zahid, Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir, Umno secretary-general Datuk Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
In this regard, Ahmad Zahid called on all people in Negeri Sembilan to respect and support every decision consented to by the palace.
“A calm discussion was held, and what Tuanku decided is the best decision, and the people as a whole must support what has been consented to and Tuanku’s decree,” he said.
Earlier yesterday, six new state assemblymen took their oath of office as Negeri Sembilan exco members before Tuanku Muhriz at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah.
They are Suhaimi Aini (Kota), Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir (Jeram Padang), Ridzuan Ahmad (Gemas), Abdul Fatah Zakaria (Bagan Pinang), Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil (Senaling) and Koh Kim Swee (Repah).
The appointment sees a change in administrative composition compared with the previous 10-member exco line-up following the political crisis in the state after 24 BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen reached a consensus to abide by their respective party leaderships’ decisions. — Bernama

Title: Parangs, masks and RM20,000 gone: Manjung police on the trail of four men
Article:
IPOH, Nov 28 — Police are tracking four men, believed to be Indonesian nationals, suspected of involvement in armed gang robberies and attempted housebreakings around Sitiawan and Ayer Tawar near Manjung since Thursday.
Manjung police chief ACP Hasbullah Abd Rahman said police received two reports of gang robberies and four of attempted housebreakings between Thursday and early yesterday.
He said initial investigations found the suspects wore face masks, were armed with parangs, and entered the victims’ homes early in the morning.
“The suspects then tied up the victims before fleeing with valuables such as mobile phones, watches, shoes and RM20,000 in cash,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Hasbullah said the case is being investigated under Sections 395/397 of the Penal Code for armed gang robbery, which carries a jail sentence of up to 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
The public with information is asked to contact the Manjung district police headquarters operations room at 05-688 6222, WhatsApp 017-682 8005, or visit the nearest police station to assist investigations.
In a separate case, police arrested five locals suspected of involvement in a housebreaking incident in Ipoh on September 11.
Acting Ipoh police chief Supt Mohamad Sajidan Abdul Sukor said the arrests of three men and two women aged between 29 and 55 were made between 1.30 pm and 4 pm in Ipoh on November 25.
“The operation was carried out following a housebreaking report on September 11 involving the loss of several items belonging to the complainant and his wife, including watches and jewellery.
“During the operation, police also seized two currency exchange receipts, six jewellery transaction receipts and a mobile phone believed to be linked to the case,” he said in a statement.
He said the main suspect has 53 previous records, including 39 criminal cases and 14 drug-related cases.
A urine test found the suspect positive for methamphetamine.
“Police also uncovered the main suspect’s possible involvement in another housebreaking case and a cable theft case in the Ipoh district. The main suspect has been remanded until Sunday to assist in investigations under Section 457 of the Penal Code,” he said. — Bernama
*Editor’s note: ACP stands for Assistant Commissioner of Police, while Supt stands for Superintendent.

Title: Fadhlina: Putrajaya’s early schooling aid gets parents talking to teachers, not politicians
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 28 — Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has urged Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi not to equate the distribution of Early Schooling Assistance (BAP) with the Bantuan Kasih Johor (BKJ), as the two initiatives have different contexts and rationales.
She said the distribution of BAP, which follows the school calendar, allows parents and teachers to meet face to face, rather than with the prime minister, ministers or any politicians.
“As well as making it easier for parents to receive the assistance, we want them to leave school with more than just RM200 in their hands. We want them to have a better understanding of their children’s development,” she said in a post on Threads.
She said the 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) findings showed that just 34 per cent of Malaysian pupils discussed school-related problems with their parents or guardians at least once a week, down from 46 per cent in 2022.
“This decline needs to be taken seriously,” she said.
Fadhlina said the country now faces various education challenges, including student discipline and mental health issues, which cannot be left to teachers alone and require active parental involvement.
The Nibong Tebal MP said there was no dispute over BKJ as a form of assistance for the people, but questioned the need to continue distributing it in person with politicians involved, given that the Johor State Legislative Assembly had been dissolved ahead of the state election.
She said the difficulties faced by older people, who were forced to stand in long queues and wait for hours to receive assistance, should not be overlooked, stressing that government aid should ease the public’s burden, not create further hardship.
She said the two assistance programmes had clearly different purposes and rationales, adding that Onn Hafiz should not cite BAP to justify how BKJ was distributed, which reportedly caused inconvenience to the public.
Onn Hafiz was reported to have said during the winding-up of the 2027 Johor Budget debate at the State Legislative Assembly yesterday that BAP was also being distributed in person, a method previously criticised in relation to BKJ.
She also questioned why some members of the Johor State Legislative Assembly balancing force (opposition) had changed their stance after its dissolution, despite having previously taken part in the face-to-face distribution of the assistance. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: BAP is the abbreviation for Bantuan Awal Persekolahan in Malay.

Title: Nomination day for Sarawak kicks off: GPS eyes all 82 seats, DAP going for 14
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 28 — The line-up of candidates contesting the 82 seats in the 13th Sarawak State Election will be known today as nomination takes place across the state.
The nomination process will run for one hour, from 9 am to 10 am, after which the respective returning officers will announce the official list of candidates eligible to contest.
A total of 82 nomination centres will be opened statewide to facilitate the process, marking the start of the 14-day campaign period ahead of polling on December 12.
Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg, who is defending the Gedong state seat, is scheduled to submit his nomination papers at Dewan Masyarakat Gedong.
DAP Sarawak chairman Chong Chieng Jen, who is contesting the Kota Sentosa seat, is expected at the Kota Sentosa Public Library, the nomination centre for the constituency.
Several Sarawak federal ministers are also expected to attend nomination centres in their respective parliamentary constituencies to show support for candidates.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof, who is also the Petra Jaya Member of Parliament (MP), and Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri, the Santubong MP, are scheduled to attend in support of GPS candidates.
GPS has confirmed that it will contest all 82 seats, seeking to retain the strong mandate it secured in the 12th Sarawak State Election.
The coalition, comprising Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB), Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), Parti Rakyat Sarawak (PRS) and Progressive Democratic Party (PDP), is fielding a mix of incumbents and 11 new faces.
DAP, meanwhile, has confirmed that it will contest 14 state seats, making it the only Pakatan Harapan (PH) component and the only political party based in peninsular Malaysia to take part in the election, as of Friday.
Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak (PBDS), Parti Bumi Kenyalang (PBK) and Parti Bangsa Malaysia (PBM) are also expected to field candidates, alongside independent candidates in several constituencies.
According to Election Commission (EC) statistics, 2,058,781 voters are eligible to cast their ballots, comprising 2,034,373 ordinary voters, 13,575 military personnel and their spouses, and 10,833 police personnel and their spouses.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia), on its website, forecast rain in several parts of Sarawak on Saturday morning.
For the latest updates on the 13th Sarawak State Election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/sarawak/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Political scientist Chandra Muzaffar, voice for justice and non-alignment, dies at 79
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Prominent political scientist and International Movement for a Just World (JUST) president Dr Chandra Muzaffar died yesterday at the age of 79.
Chandra was well known for his expertise in geopolitics and foreign policy, frequently offering insights into international affairs and advocating Malaysia’s non-aligned approach in navigating global conflicts.
JUST, in a statement expressing deep sadness over his passing, said further details on the funeral arrangements would be announced once available.
“Al-Fatihah. May Allah SWT shower him with His mercy and blessings, and place his soul among the righteous,” it said.
JUST also conveyed its thoughts and prayers to his family during this difficult time.
Chandra, who was born in Bedong, Kedah, on March 10, 1947, was a political scientist by training, having obtained his PhD in social sciences from the University of Singapore in 1977.
He began his academic career at Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) in 1970 before joining Universiti Malaya, where he served as professor and director of the Centre for Civilisational Dialogue from 1997 to 1999.
An advocate of human rights and social reform, he founded the multi-ethnic reform movement Aliran Kesedaran Negara (Aliran) in 1977 and served as its president until 1991, championing democracy, social justice, good governance and inter-ethnic understanding.
He was also a member of the executive committee of the Asian Human Rights Commission and served as deputy president of Parti Keadilan Nasional from 1999 to 2001.
Throughout his career, Chandra contributed to public discourse on international relations, frequently sharing his perspectives on global developments.
A prolific writer, he authored and edited numerous books, including Islamic Resurgence in Malaysia (1987), Human Rights and the New World Order (1993) and Rights, Religion and Reform (2002). — Bernama

Title: Confident but still caught: 70pc of Malaysians who meet scammers engage with them, says report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 28 — Despite nearly three in four Malaysian adults expressing confidence in their ability to recognise scams, seven in 10 who encounter a scam attempt still interact with it, highlighting a gap between perceived awareness and actual vulnerability, a report found.
Nonprofit network Global Anti-Scam Alliance, which combats online scams and fraud through research, intelligence sharing and cross-sector collaboration, said its latest survey revealed a gap between confidence and reality, noting that Malaysians’ confidence in recognising scams does not necessarily translate into safer behaviour.
The report also found that 83 per cent of Malaysian adults had encountered a scam in 2026, a figure largely unchanged from the previous year, with phone calls remaining the most common channel through which scams were encountered at 69 per cent.
It also highlighted that one in seven Malaysian parents (14 per cent) said their children aged seven to 17 had experienced at least one scam.
“Scam-recognition confidence in Malaysia skews strongly toward Millennials and Gen X (76 per cent and 78 per cent respectively) and men (75 per cent).
“By comparison, a lack of confidence is much higher among those from the Boomer generation (34 per cent), those aged 55+ (25 per cent) and women (20 per cent),” it said.
The State of Scams in Malaysia 2026 report surveyed 1,930 Malaysian adults aged 18 and above between March 16 and April 13 this year, examining how scams reach the public, how people respond to them, and their financial and emotional impact on those affected.
The report also highlighted the financial consequences of engaging with scam attempts, finding that three in 10 of those who interacted with scammers lost money, either by making payments, divulging personal information or both.
Investment and impersonation scams recorded high interaction rates, with 63 per cent and 65 per cent of participants respectively reporting encounters with such attempts.
WhatsApp and Telegram were the most commonly cited platforms for scam encounters, with 67 per cent and 40 per cent of respondents respectively reporting encounters on the messaging apps.
“Overall, 76 per cent of scam attempts in the past 12 months took place on platforms with direct messaging functions,” it said.
Scam prevention
Despite the high number of scam encounters, the report found that public awareness and vigilance played an important role in preventing people from becoming victims.
It said the most common reasons Malaysians gave for avoiding scam attempts were that the messages did not seem legitimate (45 per cent) or appeared too good to be true (43 per cent).
Other reasons included being educated on warning signs (41 per cent) and having a general rule of not responding to unsolicited messages or calls (40 per cent).
“Similar intuitive reasons were cited for why scam interactions did not result in financial or personal data losses, with 39 per cent saying the offers appeared too good to be true, while 37 per cent found requests for money suspicious,” it said.
The report also found that public awareness campaigns and advertisements were the most commonly cited sources of information helping Malaysian adults recognise and avoid scams, with half of all respondents identifying them as useful.
“Public awareness campaigns are the most commonly cited source of scam prevention education in Malaysia, suggesting government and public-sector efforts are helping consumers recognise and avoid scams.
“This aligns with wider perceptions that government and consumer support organisations are performing relatively well in the fight against scams, though online platforms are viewed as falling short of expectations,” it said.
Still, nearly three in 10 Malaysian adults believe public service organisations, including the government and police, bear the primary responsibility for protecting them from scams.
“The police lead in scam prevention and resolution, particularly through education (62 per cent), ease of reporting (58 per cent) and enforcement (55 per cent),” it said.
Regarding the role of financial institutions, nearly half of Malaysian adults (45 per cent) believe banks should always reimburse scam victims, while 78 per cent support banks blocking transactions above a certain value if they suspect the transactions are linked to a scam.
