Title: RMAF drug smuggling probe: Another air force officer, four civilians held as arrests hit 18
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Another Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officer and four civilians were arrested yesterday to assist in investigations into a drug smuggling syndicate that exploited military assets.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the latest arrests brought the total number of suspects detained to 18.
He said the arrests followed continued intelligence gathering and questioning of 13 suspects detained earlier in efforts to identify the masterminds behind the drug trafficking activities.
“The 29-year-old RMAF officer, who is stationed in Tawau, Sabah, was arrested within the compound of the Central Zone Criminal Investigation Branch office at Subang Air Base in Selangor at about 6.40 pm yesterday,” he said in a statement today.
Following the arrest, Hussein said Bukit Aman NCID conducted several raids across the Klang Valley at about 10.20 pm, arresting three local men aged between 26 and 28 and a 30-year-old Chinese national.
He said checks revealed that the three local suspects each had one or two previous criminal records, with one of them previously detained under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.
“Of the 18 suspects arrested, comprising eight RMAF officers and personnel and 10 civilians, eight were charged in courts in Kuala Lumpur and Selangor today under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
“Five suspects remain on remand, while further investigations and intelligence gathering continue to identify the masterminds and other individuals involved in the syndicate’s operations,” he said.
The cross-border drug smuggling operation came to light after 96.64 kg of suspected methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million and 6.98 kg of chemicals were discovered just before they were to be loaded onto an RMAF aircraft at Subang Air Base.
The discovery prompted a series of raids in the Klang Valley, Labuan and at an air base in Tawau, leading to the arrests.
The syndicate is believed to have been active since July this year, using military air transport facilities to smuggle drugs from Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah for onward distribution to international markets, including the Philippines and Indonesia. — Bernama

Title: Grab replaces flat commission model, says drivers deserve pay for pickup distance
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Nov 27 — Grab Malaysia is moving away from a one-size-fits-all commission model, saying e-hailing drivers should be paid for the time and distance they spend travelling to pick up passengers, not just for the trips they complete.
Grab Malaysia executive director Rashid Shukor said the revised Grab Service Fee (GSF) structure takes pickup time and distance into account when calculating the fee charged to drivers, with the aim of improving their earnings without raising passenger fares.
“We want to make sure we fairly compensate the driver to the best of our ability,” he said at a briefing today.
Under the previous arrangement, Grab charged a fixed 30 per cent commission regardless of how far drivers had to travel to collect passengers.
Rashid said this had long been a concern among drivers, who argued that they spent time and fuel reaching passengers but still received the same pay.
Using the example of a RM10 fare, he explained that under the revised model, the passenger’s fare would stay the same, but Grab’s service fee would vary depending on how far the driver had to travel to the pickup point.
A driver already near the passenger would pay a higher service fee, while one coming from farther away would pay less, keeping a larger share of the fare.
“In an extreme case where a driver had to travel from considerably further away to fulfil a booking, the service fee could turn negative, meaning the driver would receive more than the passenger’s fare for that trip,” Rashid said.
He added that the change was meant to cover the part of a journey that drivers previously felt went unpaid.
“The driver could be here, the fare that’s calculated, whether it’s RM15, RM10, whatever, that you pay only calculates from your pickup point to your drop-off point. It doesn’t account for this,” he said, referring to the distance travelled before reaching the passenger.
He said the revised structure could also improve driver productivity by encouraging them to accept bookings they might previously have turned down because of the extra pickup distance.
On the results of the proof of concept (POC), Rashid said drivers who opted into the revised structure earned more than 5 per cent more than those who did not take part.
He said the POC was approved by the Transport Ministry in August 2024 and had been running for about two years.
Beyond the commission percentage
Rashid said driver earnings should not be judged solely by the percentage platforms deduct, as actual income also depends on the number of trips completed, incentives, bonuses and working hours.
He said Grab focuses on the stability of drivers’ weekly earnings rather than on whether the commission on any single trip is higher or lower.
“Ultimately, whether it’s higher or lower, what we really anchor on is the stability of the driver’s earnings,” he said.
He added that keeping earnings stable required the platform to keep investing in drivers, generating passenger demand and improving the efficiency of its services.
These investments include driver incentives and bonuses during festive periods, weekends and other peak periods, as well as regulatory costs such as permits, reimbursements for Public Service Vehicle (PSV) licences, vehicle inspections and medical examinations.
Grab also provides upskilling programmes, discounts on fuel, lubricants and vehicle maintenance, personal accident insurance and compensation for certain incidents involving passengers.
Rashid said the platform had also invested in marketing, promotions, maintaining its technology and developing new features that benefit both drivers and passengers.
“Grab has also been working to improve driver flexibility while ensuring passengers could continue relying on its services.
“One feature gives drivers a window of time to decide whether to accept a booking, while another allows post-trip adjustments when journeys take longer than initially estimated.
“For example, a journey initially expected to take 30 minutes could stretch to 45 minutes because of heavy traffic or rain, with the adjustment allowing drivers to receive additional compensation for the longer trip,” he said.
He said Grab was also expanding its services to create more earning opportunities, including rides to public transport stations, group rides, Grab Assist for persons with disabilities and women-only rides.
These services benefit passengers while creating more work for drivers, he said.
He also highlighted opportunities from cross-border taxi services between Johor Baru and Singapore, as well as the shift to electric vehicles.
Making driver earnings more transparent
Rashid said Grab had also redesigned its earnings statement after drivers said they wanted a clearer picture of how much they earned and how much the platform deducted.
The new weekly statement breaks down individual bookings, earnings, incentives and bonuses, allowing drivers to assess their income over a whole week rather than trip by trip.
He said this would help drivers decide whether to take on more bookings or whether they had earned enough for the week.
Separately, Grab said in a statement today that more than 170,000 driver-partners had opted into its updated earnings structure, earning over 5 per cent more for every minute worked than before.
The company said it also maintained safeguards to discourage repeated cancellations, reduce empty travel and uphold safety standards for all users.
“Our goal is to preserve the flexibility that draws people to the gig economy while ensuring fair, transparent working conditions.
“When we support driver-partners to earn sustainably, we create a healthier marketplace where Malaysians can count on a safe, affordable ride whenever they need one,” Rashid said.

Title: Labuan Customs seizes RM18.83m in smuggled goods this year, cars taken off duty-free island top the list
Article:
LABUAN, Nov 27 — The Labuan branch of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) has recorded a total of 167 smuggling-related cases involving seizures, with an estimated value including duties and taxes of RM18.83 million, from Jan 1 to Nov 15 this year.
Labuan Customs director Saidin Jalaludin said the department conducted 12 enforcement operations during the period, including five special operations targeting vehicles, cigarettes, alcoholic beverages, drugs and other commodities.
He said the overall seizures comprised 66 vehicles, 116,396 sticks of kretek cigarettes, six electronic cigarette devices, 1,454 kilogrammes (kg) of tobacco and 187,518.92 litres of alcoholic beverages.
The department also confiscated 7.74 grammes of cannabis, 15 kg of ketum and 15 millilitres of methylenedioxy methamphetamine (MDMA), with all drug-related cases detected through the scanning of courier consignments at Labuan Airport.
Saidin said the five special operations accounted for nearly RM4.96 million in seizures, inclusive of duties and taxes, with vehicles suspected of violating tax exemption conditions applicable to the duty-free island accounting for the bulk of the amount.
“Three vehicle-focused operations, namely Op Radu, Op Radu Bersepadu and Op 90 Plus, resulted in the confiscation of 25 vehicles worth RM4.85 million, including duties and taxes.
“The modus operandi involved vehicles taken out of duty-free Labuan under the 90-day tax exemption facility but which remained outside the island beyond the permitted period, as well as vehicles smuggled out without the department’s approval,” he said at a press conference at the Kiansam Encorcement Division Complex here today.
Saidin said investigations revealed some vehicles had remained outside Labuan for more than two years, far exceeding the permitted 90-day period, with several traced to locations as far away as Kuching, Sarawak.
The department also uncovered cases involving vehicles bearing falsified registration numbers in an apparent attempt to mislead enforcement officers and evade detection.
He said Op Radu, conducted throughout Sabah in February, resulted in the seizure of nine vehicles valued at RM895,000, while Op Radu Bersepadu, carried out in Sabah and Sarawak in June, saw 12 vehicles confiscated, amounting to RM2.67 million.
“Another four vehicles worth RM1.28 million were seized during Op 90 Plus, conducted in selected areas of Sarawak this month,” he said.
Meanwhile, Op Gembleng, jointly conducted with the Labuan Health Department’s Pharmacy Division in April, recorded 26 cases following 40 inspections at courier company premises.
The operation resulted in the confiscation of cosmetic and pharmaceutical products worth RM2,387, suspected of contravening provisions under the Customs Act 1967, Poisons Act 1952 and Sale of Drugs Act 1952.
Saidin said the products were purchased through e-commerce platforms or other online channels and brought into Labuan without the necessary regulatory approvals.
In October, Op Samudera conducted by the department’s Marine Unit in waters surrounding Labuan and along Sabah’s west coast uncovered three cases involving 28,000 sticks of cigarettes and 1,480.08 litres of alcoholic beverages, valued at RM109,811.63, inclusive of duties and taxes.
He said the cases involved suspected offences under Section 135(1)(d) of the Customs Act 1967 for knowingly possessing or keeping uncustomed or prohibited goods, while the maritime cases also involved Section 135(1)(e) of the same Act for knowingly transporting or removing such goods.
Saidin urged the public to cooperate with the department in combating smuggling activities and refraining from involvement in such offences.
“Smuggling not only deprives the country of revenue but also poses a threat to national security and the well-being of the people,” he added.
Members of the public with information on smuggling activities are encouraged to contact the Customs toll-free hotline at 1-800-88-8855 or the nearest Customs office, with the department assuring that the identities of informants would be kept confidential. — Bernama

Title: Two ex-Pahang state secretariat staff jailed for slipping names into Datuk award list
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 27 — The Sessions Court here today found two former staff members of the Pahang State Secretary’s Office (SUK) guilty of unauthorised modification of the state’s awards and medals management system website six years ago.
Judge Azman Mustapha sentenced Mohd Isa Mohd Yusof, 40, to five years’ imprisonment on 26 charges, while Amer Syafeeq Aziz, 34, received two years’ jail on two charges.
The court ordered both accused to serve their sentences concurrently.
In his judgement, Azman said the defence presented by both accused amounted to a bare denial. The user IDs and passwords to access the website had been given to them and were under their control. No evidence showed that other parties had used the accounts.
“Their claim that someone else could have accessed the system at the time, which required passwords automatically saved on the computer to be used by others, was nothing more than mere assumption.
“The first and second accused had each carried out the data modifications as charged,” he said.
However, Judge Azman allowed the application by Mohd Isa, who currently works as a general assistant at the Department of Mineral and Geoscience, and Amer Syafeeq, an enforcement officer at the Kuantan City Council, for a stay of execution of the sentence.
The court fixed bail at RM130,000 for Mohd Isa and RM10,000 for Amer Syafeeq, with one surety each.
Earlier, counsel Mohamad Hamizey Mat Taib, representing Mohd Isa, appealed for a minimum fine on all charges, submitting that his client supports a wife and two children and earns RM2,600 a month.
“This case did not result in any financial loss to any government institution in Pahang, and on that basis, the accused pleads for the minimum fine to be imposed,” he said.
Datuk Zaharman Zainal Abidin, representing Amer Syafeeq, also appealed for a similar sentence, submitting his client supports a wife and three children aged between one and six, and earns between RM1,700 and RM2,000 a month.
“As a consequence of today’s conviction, the accused risks losing the job he has only recently secured,” he said.
However, Deputy Public Prosecutor Fathin Nadhirah Kasim urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence as the offences committed by both accused were serious.
“The accused did not commit the offence just once, but repeatedly. The first accused inserted 26 names into the system and modified them without authority, and even worse, the second accused was a civil servant at the time, attached to the Protocol Unit of the Pahang State Secretary’s Office,” she said.
On Dec 28, 2022, Mohd Isa and Amer Syafeeq pleaded not guilty to charges of unauthorised modification of the contents of the Pahang state awards and medals management system website between Feb 19, 2020, and Oct 12, 2021.
Mohd Isa was charged with inserting the names of 26 individuals into the website as recipients of Datuk and Datuk Seri titles from the Sultan of Pahang when they were not listed to receive the awards, while Amer Syafeeq was charged with committing a similar offence involving the names of three individuals.
They were charged under Section 5(1) of the Computer Crimes Act 1997, punishable under Section 5(4) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum fine of RM100,000, imprisonment for up to seven years, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Sandakan facing days of water rationing after power disruptions hit four treatment plants
Article:
SANDAKAN, Nov 27 — Power supply disruptions and fluctuations have affected operations at four major water treatment plants (WTP) in Sandakan, resulting in water rationing in several areas due to limited production and storage capacity.
Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee chairman Datuk Walter Kenson said the affected plants were Segaliud, Kinabatangan, Sibuga and Hilltop, with water rationing expected to continue for several days.
He said Sabah Electricity Sandakan was working to restore power through local power stations in Libaran, Batu Sapi, Labuk, Seguntor and Mowtas. However, their limited capacity was insufficient to meet overall demand, making electricity rationing unavoidable.
Walter said the committee would maintain close communication with Sabah Electricity and the Sabah Water Department in Sandakan to monitor restoration efforts and identify assistance needed to minimise the impact on residents.
“Residents are advised to conserve water, store it in clean, covered containers when supply resumes, use electricity prudently and unplug sensitive or unused electrical appliances,” he said in a statement today.
Walter, who is also Sandakan Municipal Council president, apologised on behalf of the committee for the inconvenience caused to residents.
“I fully understand the impact on the community, particularly senior citizens, children, school students, patients and business operators who rely on electricity and water for their daily needs,” he said.
He also expressed concern for Form Five students sitting for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination, urging them to remain patient and calm while encouraging parents and the community to provide support.
Residents were also urged to prioritise those in need, refrain from spreading unverified information and refer to official channels of Sabah Electricity, the Sabah Water Department and the Sandakan District Disaster Management Committee for updates.
The disruption, which occurred at 6.04am yesterday, affected two transmission circuits supplying electricity from Sabah’s West Coast to the East Coast, disrupting power supply in eight districts and affecting 153,599 registered consumers.
Sabah Electricity is targeting to fully restore electricity supply by Dec 2 or earlier.
The public can follow the latest updates via Sabah Electricity Careline’s official Facebook page or contact its hotline at 15444 or 088-515000, or WhatsApp 019-8525427. — Bernama

Title: Anwar: Masjid Warisan must embody Islamic heritage, Malay culture and Malaysian identity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Masjid Warisan, to be built in Jalan Davis here, must serve as a symbol of collective pride, blending Islamic heritage, Malay culture and Malaysian identity through architecture that complements modern development, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said the mosque should be more than just a place of worship, serving to showcase the country’s rich cultural heritage amid the capital’s rapid development and advances in technology and architecture.
“So, we want to bring together the Islamic, Malay and Malaysian legacies with modern technology. We want this mosque to be magnificent, but it must also serve a meaningful purpose,” he said when launching the project here today.
Also present were Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.
Anwar said the mosque’s development should incorporate architectural elements that reflect the beauty of its heritage, with due consideration for new technologies, environmental sustainability and the surrounding landscape.
“So, hopefully, all of you, especially the children, will feel proud when you see the design and architecture of this building.
“This means that our children will learn about new technologies, the environment, ecology and green concepts while gaining an appreciation of their own heritage,” he said.
Anwar also proposed that the mosque grounds include a water retention feature that could function as a landscaped lake, in view of Kuala Lumpur’s flood risk and to enhance the area’s aesthetic value.
He suggested that the mosque’s structure be made slightly taller to ensure it stands out as a landmark, given its location surrounded by skyscrapers in the Tun Razak Exchange (TRX) area.
“I want Masjid Warisan to be a magnificent mosque in the Federal Territory,” he said.
The Prime Minister expressed hope that the mosque would not only become a new landmark in the capital but also showcase Islamic, Malay and Malaysian heritage and identity that younger generations could take pride in, demonstrating how technological advancement can go hand in hand with the preservation of culture and history.
The mosque construction project, which occupies a 1.86-hectare site in Jalan Davis here, has received an allocation of RM4.1 million for preliminary works approved under the 2027 Second Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP).
The project is being implemented by the Federal Territories Islamic Religious Council (MAIWP) in collaboration with the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) Kulliyyah of Architecture and Environmental Design (KAED) through the MAIWP-KAED IIUM Student Design Competition, which drew the participation of 70 university students. — Bernama

Title: ‘A betrayal of the nation’: Anwar condemns alleged drug smuggling using RMAF aircraft
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described the alleged use of a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) aircraft for drug smuggling as a serious betrayal of national security, stressing that such actions will not be tolerated.
He said border security breaches and the misuse of strategic government assets were among the key issues discussed at today’s Cabinet meeting, following earlier revelations of drug smuggling activities involving commercial flights.
Anwar stressed that the government viewed the threat posed by organised crime, which he said had become deeply entrenched and systemic over several decades, with utmost seriousness and could no longer be treated as an isolated case.
“How can we allow our national defence assets to be compromised and breached by irresponsible individuals? This is an act of betrayal against the nation, and the danger it poses is immense,” he told reporters after performing Friday prayers at the Bandar Baru Ampang Mosque here today.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said he had received assurances from Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail and Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin that strict monitoring and firm action would be implemented immediately.
He added that clear directives had been issued to all enforcement agencies, including relevant departments under the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Ministry of Defence, the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), and the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM), to submit comprehensive reports on the matter.
“This has been happening for decades, and it was allowed to continue, at times through collusion with certain parties. I understand why this has caused frustration among some people.
“I want to make it clear that as long as I hold this position and carry this responsibility and trust, I will not tolerate such actions,” he said.
Anwar said that despite the government recording the highest number of enforcement actions in recent years, leakages remained a persistent problem.
He added that the Cabinet had unanimously agreed to pursue comprehensive measures to eliminate such practices.
On Nov 17, 11 individuals, comprising five RMAF personnel and six civilians, were arrested during operations in the Klang Valley and Labuan over suspected involvement in drug smuggling activities using RMAF assets.
Police also seized 96.64 kilogrammes of suspected crystal methamphetamine (syabu), estimated to be worth RM4.83 million, along with 6.98 kilogrammes of chemical substances during the operations. — Bernama

Title: Women’s Ministry reviewing child marriage as calls grow for under-18 marriage ban
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is carrying out two studies related to child marriage in Malaysia, which are expected to be completed early next year.
The ministry said the first study was being conducted in collaboration with the United Nations Children’s Fund (Unicef) Malaysia to assess the effectiveness of the implementation of the 2020-2025 National Strategic Plan to Address the Causes of Underage Marriage.
The second study is being conducted through the Malaysian Social Institute (ISM) and is titled “Study on Underage Marriage in Malaysia: Risk Factors, Protective Factors and Prevention Strategies”.
“The studies are designed to assess the implementation of strategies by the agencies involved, identify risk and protective factors, as well as examine implementation gaps and preventive measures that need to be strengthened.
“The findings will then be used to determine more focused and evidence-based follow-up measures,” it said in a written reply published on the Parliament website.
The KPWKM was replying to a question from Pang Hok Liong (PH-Labis), who wanted to know whether the government was ready to enact legislation to ban all marriages involving girls aged below 18 without exception.
It said that once both studies were completed, the ministry would use their findings to identify implementation gaps, set priorities for follow-up actions with the relevant agencies and assess specific resource requirements.
“This approach will ensure that efforts to prevent child marriage are supported by measures that address the educational, protection, well-being and participation needs of girls, in line with the theme of International Day of the Girl Child 2026, ‘End child marriage and invest in girls’ rights!’,” it added.
While the two studies are being carried out, the ministry said that efforts to address child marriage would continue through the National Child Policy and Action Plan 2026-2030.
In terms of girls’ rights, it said the government’s focus included ensuring their access to and retention in education, access to appropriate information and healthcare services, protection from violence and exploitation, as well as support for families facing socioeconomic difficulties.
“These areas are important to reduce factors that can increase the risk of child marriage,” it added.
The KPWKM also said the views and experience of girls would be taken into account when planning and improving measures that affect their lives. — Bernama

Title: MCMC takes down over 367,000 scam, fake and deepfake posts since 2024
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 27 — A total of 367,537 pieces of harmful content involving online scams, fake accounts, and manipulated imagery, including deepfakes, were removed by service providers following requests from the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) between Jan 1, 2024, and Sept 15, 2026.
In a written response published on the Parliament website, the Ministry of Communications stated that 13,234 or 92 per cent of the 14,392 deepfake-related items reported during the period had been removed. Similarly, 50,432 (87.6 per cent) of the 57,600 pieces of fake content were taken down.
The highest removal rate involved scam-related content, including fake accounts and impersonation, with 303,871 of the 316,215 reported items (96.1 per cent) successfully removed.
“Five requests for the removal of content related to financial scams were submitted to licensed service providers under the Online Safety Act 2025 [Act 866], and all such content has been removed,” the ministry stated.
The ministry provided the information in response to a question from Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson), who sought details on the volume of deepfakes, fake accounts, and digital scams removed, as well as the mechanisms in place to prevent the spread of such content.
The ministry added that the MCMC proactively monitors social media platforms to identify misuse and strengthens cooperation with service providers and law enforcement agencies to expedite the detection and removal of content that violates the law.
“The government emphasises that efforts to address harmful content cannot be merely reactive.
“Therefore, through the enforcement of Act 866, service providers are also held accountable for implementing preventive and risk-mitigation measures at the platform level to curb the spread of harmful content and safeguard user safety,” it said.
The ministry also disclosed that the MCMC began enforcing the Risk Mitigation Code (RMC) on June 1 this year under Act 866, requiring licensed service providers to introduce preventive measures at the platform level, including labelling and tagging content generated or manipulated using artificial intelligence (AI).
On enforcement actions under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) during the same period, the ministry reported that 18 cases involving false content had been brought to court, while 32 cases had resulted in compound fines. Another 68 cases had received warning letters, and 30 remained under investigation.
In a separate response to Wan Razali Wan Nor (PN-Kuantan), the Ministry of Communications clarified that a more progressive approach to film censorship by the National Film Development Corporation Malaysia (FINAS) did not mean an unrestricted relaxation of existing regulations.
Instead, the approach focuses on assessing film content based on its narrative context, artistic value, and suitability for different age groups, while taking into account religious and racial sensitivities and the prevailing norms of Malaysian society.
The ministry also clarified that content on Over-the-Top (OTT) digital streaming platforms remains subject to the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Content Code, under the oversight of the MCMC.
Meanwhile, in response to a question from Mohd Azizi Abu Naim (Gua Musang), the ministry reported that internet and communications coverage in populated areas of Kelantan had reached 99.88 per cent as of Sept 1, supported by the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA).
5G coverage in the state’s populated areas had also reached 96.9 per cent through Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) and 95.3 per cent through U Mobile Sdn Bhd.
Under the government’s “Where There Is a Road, There Is Internet” initiative, work to improve connectivity along expressways commenced last August, while implementation along major roads is scheduled to begin early next year.
Addressing the challenges of providing internet access in rural areas, the ministry said the MCMC would continue assessing the suitability of satellite technologies, including Very Small Aperture Terminal High Throughput Satellite (VSAT HTS) and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites.
The assessment would take into account local requirements, technical feasibility, and funding availability, it said. — Bernama

Title: No deals with US-blacklisted firms, Malaysian companies told after Cabinet briefing on chip curbs
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry (Miti) has briefed the Cabinet on United States semiconductor export restrictions, and Malaysian companies have been told not to deal with firms on Washington’s trade blacklist, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the directive follows Washington’s addition on November 23 of Singapore-based Megaspeed International and six affiliates in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand to its Entity List over suspected diversion of Nvidia artificial intelligence (AI) chips to China.
“The Miti minister informed the Cabinet that Malaysian companies had been directed not to conduct any transactions with companies blacklisted by the US to avoid complications in their business and trade dealings,” Fahmi said in his weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing.
On a separate matter, Communications Minister Fahmi Fadzil said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission’s (MCMC) legal action against Google would not jeopardise the US technology giant’s planned US$15 billion (RM61 billion) investment in Malaysia.
Fahmi said regulatory compliance and foreign investment were separate matters, adding that the government’s priority was to ensure Malaysians were protected from harmful online content under the Online Safety Act 2025.
“Our position is that Malaysians should not be exposed to harmful content. This is a regulatory matter and has nothing to do with investment,” he said.
He added that Putrajaya hoped the dispute could be resolved amicably through the cooperation of all parties involved.
MCMC disclosed earlier this week that it had filed two separate lawsuits against Google LLC, seeking a combined RM600 million in damages over its alleged failure to adequately address harmful content on YouTube.
The first suit concerns alleged failures to tackle online gambling, scams and fraud, while the second involves the republication of content by blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, despite an interim injunction granted by the High Court on June 19.

Title: Ismail Lasim: New exco to take on multiple portfolios as Negeri Sembilan moves to clear state backlog
Article:
KUALA PILAH, Nov 27 — Each of the six newly appointed Negeri Sembilan state executive council (exco) members is expected to oversee at least two portfolios to ensure the smooth administration of the state, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
He said the allocation of portfolios was still being reviewed and would be announced within a day or two, with some portfolios likely to be combined based on their suitability and the relevance of their functions.
“For now, no portfolios have been assigned, and I am asking for a day or two to finalise them, as only six exco members have been approved as of today. We have many portfolios, so I may have to combine some of them,” he said.
Ismail said he would ensure that the exco members were assigned related portfolios to make it easier for them to carry out their duties.
He was speaking to reporters after the six exco members were sworn in before Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Seri Menanti here today.
The new exco members are Suhaimi Aini (Kota), Datuk Mohd Zaidy Abdul Kadir (Jeram Padang), Ridzuan Ahmad (Gemas), Abdul Fatah Zakaria (Bagan Pinang), Mohamad Qayyum Abd Jalil (Senaling) and Koh Kim Swee (Repah).
They replaced the 10 exco members who were removed following an administrative impasse in the state.
Ismail said the state government would focus fully on clearing all outstanding papers after exco meetings had not been held for almost two months.
“Most of the outstanding papers involve matters affecting the people. Starting as early as next week, I have scheduled exco meetings for Tuesdays and Thursdays, and possibly more frequently, to clear the backlog,” he said.
Ismail said he was considering the inclusion of women representatives in the state administration.
He also said the next exco meeting would confirm the state budget before it was presented to Tuanku Muhriz.
He will also seek his consent for the date of the State Legislative Assembly sitting, which is expected to take place this December. — Bernama

Title: Not just airports anymore: Cabinet widens anti-narcotics checks to military sites
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 27 — The Cabinet has agreed to extend anti-narcotics measures at airports to military installations, following the arrests of 13 people, including seven Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel, over a drug seizure at the Subang Air Base, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
“The 17 initiatives between the Home Ministry and Ministry of Transport at strategic locations such as airports have shown to be successful,” Fahmi told reporters at the weekly post-Cabinet press conference here.
“But the initiatives do not cover military installations like RMAF airports and so on. So the Cabinet today agreed that the initiatives will be widened to Mindef,” he added, using the abbreviation for the Ministry of Defence.
Six of those arrested, including three RMAF officers, were charged this morning at the Magistrate’s Court in Shah Alam, Selangor with trafficking 96.2kg of suspected methamphetamine at the air base.
The 17 initiatives, officially described as 17 substantive recommendations, are a phased plan to tighten security at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport and other international entry points nationwide, which the Cabinet approved in August.
They were drawn up after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Jakarta on July 29 with roughly 25kg of drugs, a case separate from the Subang airbase seizure.
The government said the joint Home Ministry and Transport Ministry framework focuses on aviation security, national security and border control, to be rolled out in three phases starting with six immediate actions.
Key measures disclosed under the plan include deploying artificial intelligence-assisted screening and body scanners, expanding narcotics sniffer-dog patrols and tightening joint police and aviation security checks on flight crew and ground staff to close insider access loopholes.

Title: Johor MB: State reins in data centre water allocations, approves 21 MLD of 73 MLD sought
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 27 — The Johor government has approved a total of 21 million litres per day (MLD) of treated water for 19 data centres operating in the state, compared with their initial applications totalling 73 MLD.
Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi said the approved allocation represented about 1.05 per cent of Johor’s average treated water production of 2,034MLD.
He said the figures showed that every data centre application submitted through the Johor State Data Centre Development Coordination Committee (JPPPDNJ) had to undergo a technical evaluation before planning permission could be granted.
As such, he dismissed claims that data centre development would lead to water supply disruptions, stressing that the people’s well-being would not be sacrificed for the sake of investment.
“Water supply security, including energy sufficiency and environmental sustainability, are matters that cannot be compromised at all,” he said when winding up Johor’s Budget 2027 debate at the Johor State Legislative Assembly sitting at Bangunan Sultan Ismail here today.
Onn Hafiz, who is also Machap state assemblyman, said that apart from controlling the volume of water allocated, the state government was also encouraging data centres to adopt water-cooling technologies and alternative water sources to reduce their reliance on conventional water supplies.
He said companies that had taken such initiatives included Bridge Data Centres and Computility, which used treated wastewater.
“DayOne, meanwhile, uses water from Sungai Tehran through its own water treatment plant built at the Kempas Tech Park,” he said.
Meanwhile, Onn Hafiz said Johor had become a preferred destination for high-profile investors, especially in high-tech and high-value-added industries, emphasising that the state’s development was not focused solely on data centres.
He said that 60,000 potential jobs, including 15,000 premium-paying positions, have been created through investments secured between 2024 and the third quarter of this year.
The Second Meeting of the First Session of the 16th Johor State Legislative Assembly, which began on Nov 19, ended today. — Bernama

Title: DAP adds two more Sarawak seats to stop GPS walking in unopposed
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 27 — The Democratic Action Party (DAP) has added two more seats to its 13th state election line-up in a last-minute move aimed at preventing Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) candidates from securing uncontested victories.
Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen said the decision to contest Bawang Assan and Senadin was made after PKR announced on Nov 24 that it would sit out the polls.
He said Lanang MP and Dewan Rakyat Deputy Speaker Alice Lau Kiong Yieng would contest Bawang Assan while Sarawak DAP secretary Alan Ling Sie Kiong would contest Senadin.
“The state committee has conducted a discussion and meeting and finally we decided to contest another two seats to reduce the chances of GPS candidates winning uncontested,” Chong told a press conference at DAP headquarters here.
He said the decision was made in the spirit of democracy and to give voters a choice.
“I think the voters deserve to have a choice to vote. Therefore, we added on two additional candidates to offer ourselves as a choice for a stronger check and balance of the GPS,” he said.
With the two additions, Chong said Sarawak DAP would contest 14 seats in the election.
The full line-up is Lim Nee Kon in Opar, Michael Kong Feng Nian in Padungan, Violet Yong Wui Wui in Pending, Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen in Batu Lintang and Chong himself in Kota Sentosa.
The party will also field Jordan Soo Tien Ren in Batu Kitang, Sim Kiat Leng in Batu Kawa, Roderick Wong Siew Lead in Meradong, Stanley Chiew Sung Ngie in Bukit Assek, Alice Lau Kiong Yieng in Bawang Assan, Irene Wong Lee Ting in Pelawan, Chiew Chan Yew in Tanjong Batu, Voon Kai Foo in Pujut and Ling Sie Kiong in Senadin.
Chong said the lineup had an average age of 41.42 years with two Gen Z candidates – Soo and Irene Wong – while three candidates were women.
He described the lineup as a reflection of DAP’s emphasis on youth and women’s participation in politics.
Chong also said Sarawak DAP would fight the election without the involvement of its federal ministers and deputy ministers.
“We are fighting this battle alone,” he said.
On his decision to return to Kota Sentosa after previously contesting Padungan, Chong said a land alienation issue involving about 23 acres near Sentosa Mile 7 Bazaar was among the reasons.
He claimed the land where the existing Kota Sentosa police station had stood for decades was alienated to a private company in 2022 at about RM400,000 per acre.
Chong said he had raised the matter in the State Legislative Assembly but claimed it was not answered there.
“I think this is something that we cannot tolerate. We do not want a return of the era which we have fought so hard to end in the last decade,” he said.
Chong said DAP would disclose further details on the land issue during the campaign and welcomed Kota Sentosa incumbent Wilfred Yap to respond.
On the federal decision involving PKR he said he viewed Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s position as either cooperation with or yielding to pressure from GPS chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg.
“I’ll leave it to the interpretation of an individual to make,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Dragon boats race the rain: Penang regatta starts at 8am to beat the storms this weekend
Article:
SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 27 — The Penang International Dragon Boat Regatta has moved to an 8am start this weekend to beat forecast thunderstorms and fit in more teams, Penang Tourism and Creative Economy Committee chairman Wong Hon Wai said today.
Races will start at 8am and end at about 5pm on both Saturday and Sunday, with an earlier finish possible.
“We need more time to accommodate all the 68 teams participating in the race this year,” Wong said after opening the Mahou-Meki Hobby Convention at The Ship Campus in Batu Kawan.
He said races will be suspended if heavy rain sets in and resume once it stops, with any races delayed on Saturday moved to Sunday depending on the time lost.
“We have been observing the water. It’s very calm in the mornings,” he said.
To save time, the opening ceremony has been shortened and racing will continue through it, instead of pausing for one to two hours as before, with no lunch breaks.
He said marine police and rescue boats will be on standby and participants must wear life jackets, after boats capsized at last year’s event.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast afternoon thunderstorms in most areas of Penang from November 26 to 28, while Wong said the warning he saw pointed to storms in the evening and at night.
Earlier today, Penang Housing and Environment executive councillor Datuk Seri Sundarajoo Somu urged the public to limit activities near the sea and rivers.
Wong said similar precautions will apply to the Aspen–Klippa Penang Bridge International Marathon 2026 on December 13, where the start may be delayed if there is heavy rain.
“We have prayed for good weather so we hope we will get good weather during these events,” he said.
